content.user_title: Build Durable Go Workflows with DBOS
content.value_statement: Reliable Go workflow code is hard to design across crashes, retries, and deployments. This skill gives DBOS patterns for workflows, steps, queues, clients, testing, and upgrades.
actual_capabilities: Guides DBOS context setup, workflow registration, launch, and shutdown for Go applications.
Explains workflow and step boundaries, deterministic workflows, retries, timeouts, durable sleep, and background execution.
Describes DBOS queues, including concurrency, rate limits, priority, partitioning, deduplication, and worker listening.
Covers workflow communication with messages, events, streams, and external DBOS Client usage.
Provides testing and upgrade guidance for mocks, integration tests, patching, and versioned deployments.
limitations: It does not install DBOS, create databases, or run Go commands by itself.
Examples use placeholder URLs and environment variable names that users must adapt.
It assumes familiarity with Go, context handling, and application deployment.
It summarizes DBOS patterns and may not cover every SDK release change.

use_cases.title: Build resilient backend workflows
use_cases.description: Design Go workflows that recover correctly after crashes and retries.

use_cases.title: Control async workload execution
use_cases.description: Choose queue, rate limit, partition, and priority patterns for DBOS workers.

use_cases.title: Test and upgrade DBOS services
use_cases.description: Plan mocks, integration tests, patching, and versioned deployments for workflow changes.

prompt_templates.title: Set up a DBOS Go app
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the required DBOS Go setup for a new service. Include context creation, workflow registration, launch, and shutdown.

prompt_templates.title: Move operations into steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go workflow design and identify which operations should be DBOS steps. Explain the deterministic workflow boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Design queue controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workload planning with resource limits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose DBOS queue settings for a workload with API rate limits, per-user fairness, and priority jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a safe workflow upgrade
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release planning for breaking workflow changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DBOS Go migration plan for a breaking workflow change. Include patching, versioning, testing, and retirement checks.

output_examples.input: I need to process external API calls reliably from Go.
output: Use a DBOS workflow for orchestration.
Place HTTP calls inside steps so results are checkpointed.
Add retries and queue rate limits when the API has transient failures.

output_examples.input: My workers must avoid duplicate jobs for the same customer.
output: Use queue deduplication for submitted work.
Consider partitioning when each customer needs its own concurrency limit.

output_examples.input: I need to deploy a breaking workflow change safely.
output: Use patching when in-progress workflows need the old path.
Use application versions for blue-green deployment.
Wait for old workflow runs to drain before removing compatibility paths.

best_practices: Register workflows and queues before launching the DBOS application.
Keep workflows deterministic and move external side effects into steps.
Use queues, retries, and timeouts to control resource use and failure recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not start workflows from inside steps.
Do not place non-deterministic API calls directly inside workflow logic.
Do not deploy breaking workflow changes without patching or versioning guidance.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Go applications that use DBOS durable workflows, steps, queues, and communication patterns.

faq.question: Does it run DBOS commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users decide which commands or code changes to apply.

faq.question: Does it cover workflow testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains mock-based unit tests and integration tests with a real Postgres database.

faq.question: Can it help with queue design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers concurrency, rate limiting, deduplication, partitioning, priority, and worker listening patterns.

faq.question: Does it explain DBOS Client usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers client setup and external enqueue operations for applications outside a DBOS process.

faq.question: Is it specific to Go?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples and guidance target the DBOS Go SDK.
